checks_collection: GitHub REST check-runs filter=all and final-head metadata, read non-atomically after cutoff

provenance.cohort: Workflow CI pull_request runs, paginated fixed windows. Search updated devel PRs and join their latest observed head SHA and same-repo head branch to the runs. Pick midpoint ranks in chronological order per period/path stratum, up to 25 Agentplane backend or test heads and 12 other heads. Read all check-run pages for each exact head, latest check record per required context by check ID. GitHub timestamps have one-second resolution. Latest observed head can differ from the head at cutoff. Workflow run status is a separate denominator with re-runs, fork markers and superseded runs. Path class uses current PR files only when they correspond to the exact SHA.
provenance.clocks: Earliest CI workflow creation in the frame for each exact SHA through the latest accepted required check completion. Job created-to-start includes orchestration and runner dispatch. Receipt, historical push and eligibility require independent clocks.
provenance.runner_census: Used collect.py fixed-window runs and its all-attempt pagination helper. The older active-run sweep raced (26 reported, 14 returned). The clipped sample omits earlier runs and unfinished jobs. Pre-commit, artifact and Test & Build roles use GitHub-hosted Linux runners; outer Remote Bazel uses BuildBuddy. Stable owner-wide capacity is unknown.
provenance.native: CI deterministic test invocation IDs per workflow run and attempt. GetExecution NEW-origin physical TestRunner rows, deduplicated by execution ID, and distinct process and CPU units. Critical paths and exact trace outputs sampled for named cases only. Native action last completion is a screening statistic; recorded Bazel critical path is shown where retrieved. Selected VM and Firecracker trace warm/cold status is independent of cache reuse of the whole action.
provenance.routing: Representative action and command digests decoded for PR #18244. Synthetic test commits fetched from Git database; first parent checked for KVM cutover and Firecracker reuse ancestry; second parent equals measured head. The rollout PR itself includes its own routing change on its head.
provenance.metrics: Mimir builtin dashboard series selectors, filter to up scrapes; 60-second steps. The task gauge includes preparation and upload. Missing task values are omitted. Local reservations can repeat a physical request. CPU measurements use 2-minute rate. Work filesystem follow-up uses /buildbuddy.
provenance.censoring: Fork and non-devel eligibility, exact push time, first API observation, installation/inbox/webhook delivery and agent reads are outside this retained-head analysis. Final latest checks are observed after the sampling window and capture recovery. Earlier PR heads stay in the workflow run counts but do not have exact gate timelines in this snapshot.

gate_headroom.clock: Gate offsets are elapsed seconds from each head's labeled workflow-start proxy, as supplied in the reviewed input.
gate_headroom.assumption: Scenarios subtract the stated seconds from observed gate offsets, clipping each at zero, while holding other gate clocks and dependency structure fixed; adjusted completion order may change. This is a conditional upper-bound sensitivity, not a treatment effect or actual auto-merge readiness; do not add worker or CPU times.

prior_baseline.open: Two-worker floor causal benefit; fleet fixture reuse; 30% or four-minute end-to-end design.

rerun_causes.18106: Gateway crash case saw environment STATE_NOT_READY on typed process read; teardown also reported an unsettled model exchange. Firecracker and VM both passed after long input fetch.
rerun_causes.18243: Provider I/O test returned the typed timeout but never observed its blocked-body Read method start. Its timeout starts 25ms before the real transport has proven a body read.
rerun_causes.18254: Managed Pod-platform action failed provider Firecracker snapshot restore with TSC scaling EINVAL, before reaching the test body.
rerun_causes.18256: Restart case reconnected and received a snapshot whose last cursor equaled the prior cursor. Strict growth assertion failed.
rerun_causes.18273: One PID1 container-test shard reached its timeout; target was green on retry. Early indexed first-failure query returned an empty label for this timeout.

rerun_request_clock: All five GitHub attempt metadata records identify User-type triggering accounts. Provenance cannot distinguish direct user action from a client acting as that identity. Prior red-to-next-job-creation elapsed 32, 93, 253, 661 and 663 seconds. Next-job assignment was 2–8 seconds.

input_fetch_case.qualification: Matching file counts/bytes and overlapping native phase timestamps suggest shared input or transfer pressure. Stats do not identify the CAS object, edge cache, or transfer bottleneck. The cluster OCI mirror is configured for image pulls, a different path from Bazel CAS action input staging.

From the sampled CI workflow creation to the first observed success of all three required check names in their original workflow runs. managed_pod_admission.counterfactual: Fixed observed enqueue, preparation, process, upload, other actions, other gates and post-test work. Removing this queue can advance the observed path at most to the latest unchanged physical completion or next required gate. Applies only where the Pod critical path was verified. This is a queue-only ceiling, not measured savings or a population estimate.

worker_signals.counter_method: Maximum fleet-wide two-minute increase sampled at one minute. Prometheus extrapolates counts. Canceled RPCs can result from client cancellation. Use logs and native execution records for exact per-action evidence.

provenance.file_mapping: Decode downloadedFileIndicesBitmap on completed TestRunners against CAS Action input Directory tree in executor traversal order. One blob may serve multiple paths. Counts and bytes reconcile against native IO receipts.

cas_followup.replay_method: Loopback proxy with empty Pebble store, live BuildBuddy Cloud upstream and bb download using the same four exact PR digests. SHA-256 and length verified for all successful reads. Metrics sampled before initial fill and after warm repetition. CLI call wall includes verification.
cas_followup.replay_scope: Single developer host. Two independent read sets in the warm phase. Desktop-route upstream was healthy. Production KVM canary and account pricing or support entitlement are unmeasured.

rows.label: Serial, one case at a time

initial_discard.discard_attempt_cause: BuildBuddy scheduler could not find the requested executor. Kubernetes had replaced the original worker and its current VM, VMI and blank work disk are newer than the serial run.

firecracker_overlap.finding: The matched warm pair ran both cases and they passed. The case lifetimes overlapped for 53.7s. The concurrent TestRunner process was 69.8s faster than the serial process. The interval covering both cases was 66.3s shorter.
firecracker_overlap.method: The last two timed rows reused one warm worker, Docker runner and K3s data mount. The concurrent action was sent to that executor with a scheduler override. All four action input roots agree. The only TestRunner command change was the case limit. Both original case implementations and their own cleanup ran on one stack. The spike omitted supplemental native diagnostics on scenario failures.
firecracker_overlap.limit: The initial concurrent attempt landed on a different worker and started cold. Its process time cannot estimate the concurrency effect. The cgroup memory peak spans the runner lifetime and only detects a new high water mark. GitHub feedback is unmeasured.
firecracker_overlap.decision: The warm pair supports a coverage-preserving implementation experiment. Run a matched cold comparison and repeat across workers before estimating the effect on required CI.
firecracker_overlap.action: Validate the overlap implementation on cold fixtures and more KVM workers.

staggered_probe.finding: Staggering changed which pod waited. The live-guest pod reached PodScheduled in 3–4 seconds after creation, while proxy-trust waited 157–158 seconds. The staggered TestRunner took 302 and 284 seconds. That spread covers both the 285.5-second simultaneous control and much of the distance to the 303-second serial control.
staggered_probe.scheduler_evidence: The nested node advertised four CPUs and one KVM slot. Each launcher requested 2.01 CPUs including its sidecar and one KVM slot. The scheduler reported Insufficient cpu and Insufficient devices.kubevirt.io/kvm for the waiting pod. This establishes the scheduler’s placement constraint in the tested fixture.
staggered_probe.action: Keep required CI serial on the current fixture. If overlap is revisited, first measure a fixture with enough CPU and KVM capacity for both launchers and include full setup and teardown.

kvm_work_disk_trial.finding: Keep the production pool on SSD. Cold HDD took 2.81× as long as SSD. With warm worker caches and a fresh fixture, HDD took 1.95× as long.
kvm_work_disk_trial.method: One active worker at a time on the same wyrm2 host. The worker image, resources, 80 GiB work disk and complete Bazel action were matched. Each cell is one run of both VM scenarios.
kvm_work_disk_trial.clocks: From TestRunner execution start to completion. Worker start-to-Ready was 267s on SSD and 309s on HDD. Cold nested imports took 199.1s and 876.5s. The underlying data preserves worker preparation, input fetch, guest readiness and shutdown spans. Required CI's retained fixture and PR feedback time remain unmeasured for this storage comparison.

images.note: The 25 images contain 2.43 GiB of unique layer blobs. About 2.20 GiB is uncompressed tar and 239 MiB is gzip. The 25 image totals reuse some blobs. Each import clock includes streaming and containerd snapshot work.

full.method: The OCI manifests and SHA256-validated CAS file receipts describe the exact Bazel input tree. Layer bytes use each blob's stored TAR or gzip representation. Root filesystem allocation, gzip expansion or CAS network bytes are outside this accounting. Per-image spans time K3s import, including streaming and containerd snapshot work.

io.note: Original node-exporter scrapes about one minute apart. The durations and bytes cover only scrapes inside each phase. The evidence also includes the scrapes that bound each phase. Wyrm2 device counters include other workloads on each virtual disk. Image import sits inside TestRunner.

full.method: Differences of monotonic node-exporter counters on original Mimir scrapes. Inside uses first and last scrapes within the interval, and bracket uses the nearest before and after. Their deltas bound whole-device activity during the interval. Device accounting includes every user of that virtual device. Worker, TestRunner and image-import windows overlap.

io.qemu_note: QEMU counted 3,077,193,728 read bytes and 18,499,571,712 written bytes on the canary's own HDD work device from boot to the warm action submission. That includes worker bootstrap, the cold action and its input staging. Across the separately bracketed warm action it counted 697,199,616 read bytes and 1,684,799,488 written bytes. The QEMU counts describe the guest work disk. The table above counts all I/O on the underlying wyrm2 virtual device. These are measurements at two layers of the same path.

kvm_work_disk_trial.capacity: The KubeVirt compute container requests 8,468 MiB. OVH HDD worker memory request headroom was ovh-ns102453 4.23 GiB, ovh-ns103656 4.11 GiB, ovh-ns103711 4.90 GiB. All three had nested KVM and fell below the matched worker's memory request, so the trial stayed on wyrm2.
kvm_work_disk_trial.cleanup: Production was Ready in all 127 samples. Both canary disks and all other trial objects were removed. The HDD volume was released and detached before deletion. Its pool regained 16.48 GiB.
kvm_work_disk_trial.cleanup_receipt: Production was fully Ready in 127 of 127 samples during the monitored interval. After the final action, the canary was idle and drained. Both work claims, VMs, VolumeAttachments, runtime configuration and the trial pull secret were removed. SSD PV pvc-6b6f6e4f-a4d8-4c1a-8aab-ab6aa626c4fa reclaimed automatically. An ownership and detach check confirmed the HDD Retain PV pvc-7f559530-66ea-4c3a-97b4-5897a1e46ca0 before removing its PV and LINSTOR resource. LINSTOR showed wyrm2's HDD pool free space rise from 325.21 GiB to 341.69 GiB.

kvm_retained_vm_ssd.finding: Reusing the live K3s fixture on one isolated SSD worker cut TestRunner time by 151.7s. Work-disk writes fell from 7.79 to 1.07 GiB (86% less). Fixture setup accounted for 6.61 GiB of that difference.
kvm_retained_vm_ssd.method: Both uncached runs used the same required VM action and passed the Claude and Codex cases. The Docker process, K3s API and operators survived the handoff. The namespace, database and fixture credentials were recreated.
kvm_retained_vm_ssd.phase_note: QEMU sampled the canary work disk about every two seconds. The table uses samples inside each phase. The cold import envelope overlaps fixture setup. Worker startup includes the worker image and reaches Ready once. The container disk is outside the QEMU work-disk counters.
kvm_retained_vm_ssd.host_note: Whole-device SSD samples include concurrent wyrm2 workloads. In the cold process the node recorded 9.20 GiB written over 480s at 42.8% busy, with 5.4% node I/O PSI some. In the retained process it recorded 0.95 GiB written over 300s at 19.3% busy, with 2.9% node I/O PSI some.
kvm_retained_vm_ssd.impact: The cold fixture streamed 25 images. The retained fixture streamed none, validated 14 existing images and left 11 baseline images in place. The test still deploys workloads, runs both nested guests, and cleans up. Production was 2/2 Ready in 44 of 44 samples. The canary retained runner and work claim were removed. Fleet reuse rate, PR-feedback savings and the HDD retained path remain unmeasured.

qemu_evidence.method: QEMU vdb monotonic counters sampled about every two seconds. Interior samples give a lower bound over the corresponding wall interval. Bracketing samples include up to one sample of I/O on each side. Parent and nested phases overlap. Writes are temporal guest disk I/O, not per-file attribution or physical device writes.

node_evidence.method: Differences of monotonic node-exporter counters on original Mimir scrapes. Inside uses first and last scrapes within the interval, and bracket uses the nearest before and after. Their deltas bound whole-device activity during the interval. Device accounting includes every user of that virtual device. The TestRunner and image-import windows overlap. Node pressure includes all processes.

nov22_feedback.method: Hash sort sha256(nov22 + head SHA), first 35 per UTC creation day. Sample fixed November 15–21 inclusive. Join PR-event check suites by repository, branch and head SHA. Test current three contexts, requiring simultaneous acceptance. Checks and file metadata collected November 22 from 02:52–03:02 UTC. Edit family uses first-parent file list on single-parent commits with fewer than 100 files. Docs alongside one code family take the code family. PR-wide classification requires GitHub current head equal sampled SHA and complete list at most 100 files.

kvm_runner_dispatch.population: Two selected cold required KubeVirt actions on 22 November UTC. This follow-up does not estimate a fleet miss rate.
kvm_runner_dispatch.method: Joined BuildBuddy execution IDs and executor host IDs to Loki guest-console-log runner lookups and recycling events. Compared the K3s persistence fingerprint from each action and its warm predecessor. Mimir CPU and RAM figures are last available 60-second samples of reservations. Work-disk space is guest filesystem availability. Central scheduler offers and candidate rankings are unavailable.
kvm_runner_dispatch.worker_log_selector: {namespace="buildbuddy-executor",container="guest-console-log",app=~"buildbuddy-kvm-worker-[0-9]+"} |~ "Looking for match|Successfully recycled runner|Executor shutting down"

cases.clock_note: The VM worker clock precedes central enqueue by about one second. Compare the two central enqueue timestamps to each other.

retention_sample.method: Count guest Looking for match messages with this KubeVirt key, deduplicating duplicated console records by execution ID. Retries and cancelled attempts can each issue their own lookups. A paused platform-key match is a candidate for fixture reuse.
retention_sample.replay: At each one-minute scrape, take the maximum observed desired replica count from that sample and the previous 15 minutes, including pre-window history. Sum the 240 counts. This prices delayed scale-in on the recorded demand trace. It does not simulate HPA recommendations, VM identity, routing or elapsed PR time.

kvm_scale_up_signal.reported_count: Current VMI-owned launcher pods with up=1, registered_to_scheduler=1 and an assigned CPU sample. Those series and pool desired replicas must be younger than 180 seconds.
kvm_scale_up_signal.raw_increase_filter: Reporting equals desired, desired below eight, and sum(busy workers by positive assigned CPU) plus sum(local executor queue_length) exceeds desired. The queue falls back to zero on the absent aggregate, matching the scaler input. This is a pointwise comparison before the HPA policies.
kvm_scale_up_signal.full_size_headroom_filter: For the CPU-idle subset, match a current nondeleting worker with fresh successful health checks and scrapes, 4 unassigned estimated CPUs, 7 GiB unassigned estimated RAM, at least 50 decimal GB available on /buildbuddy and no observed positive tasks_executing stage. An absent stage is counted as zero observed. Supplied samples can carry values forward across evaluation points.

telemetry_limits.hosted_metrics: The authenticated execution metric inventory exposes the exported local queue gauge and duration metrics. No distinct pending execution count was found for the pool.

full_size_shadow_replay.method: Require desired below eight and complete current-worker coverage for registration, health, CPU, RAM and disk. Evaluate positive local reservations with no worker meeting 4 unassigned CPU, 7 GiB unassigned RAM and 50 GB filesystem thresholds. Filesystem availability is a proxy for suitability for the KubeVirt action, whose scratch request exceeds Firecracker’s 20 GB. This probe has no distinct execution IDs or shapes and does not predict scheduler admission.

method.invocation_sampling: Order distinct invocation IDs by the first matching guest-console log receipt, then take 48 evenly spaced order statistics including the endpoints across 72 IDs. Fetch native BuildBuddy executions for the two required suite labels within selected invocations and deduplicate on execution ID.
method.worker_attribution: Join each exact execution ID from the BuildBuddy record to a unique immutable launcher pod named in its executor guest-console receipt.
method.scrape_sampling: Evaluate at 30 seconds with timestamp() to recover physical scrape times. Deduplicate forwarded metric values by physical scrape time for each guest pod. Require latest pre-start scrape within 75 seconds, at least one in-window scrape, gaps of at most 75 seconds between accepted scrapes, and last in-window scrape within 75 seconds of worker completion. The minimum includes baseline. Net drop is baseline minus sampled minimum, in GiB.
method.verdict: Require COMPLETED and complete worker clocks in native records. Use bb execution get <execution_id> --output=json to verify ExecuteResponse.status.code and ExecuteResponse.result.exitCode, both zero for a pass. Read runnerMetadata.taskNumber for each pass, where 1 is first assignment to that runner and values above 1 are later assignments.
method.percentile: Nearest-rank p95, computed on per-execution values rounded to 0.001 GiB.
method.limits: A single 24-hour sample from visible runner lookups. Minute scrapes can miss short-lived peaks. Net filesystem change may mask temporary writes, concurrent guest activity and cleanup, and does not measure total bytes written. The first-assignment split is at runner level. It does not prove cold worker, image or file caches. Production worker concurrency was one and the PVC was fixed at 80 GiB.

kvm_work_disk_requirements.timed_nonzero_exit_diagnostics: The four exact test.xml artifacts show setup, HTTP 503 or teardown failures. None mentioned ENOSPC, no space left on device, DiskPressure or insufficient ephemeral storage.

shadow_threshold_sensitivity.comparison: Same exact replay and 1,441 evaluation ticks, changing only the threshold from 50 GiB to 30 GiB.

shadow_unit_sensitivity.method: Inline the proposed worker-fit expression into the shadow-target rule and query the same historical Mimir data with the decimal and binary threshold. The 30-second historical full-size headroom probe above retains its original decimal threshold.

earlier_trim_attempt.failure: Both scenarios reached pytest teardown. The trim command was absent from the Bazel test PATH and never executed. The runner followed its owned disposal path.

method.historical_examples: Sampled worker net drop comes from kvm_work_disk_requirements. The BuildBuddy test outputs storage/before-import and storage/final provide GNU df -B1 for the nested ext4 and GNU du -B1 -x for its containerd store. recycled-runner.json establishes whether each runner had a prior action.
method.transfers: BuildBuddy execution response ioStats fileDownloadSizeBytes and fileUploadSizeBytes. Largest inputs come from exact GetExecutionDownloads receipts, deduplicated by digest.
method.manual_routing: The source worktree starts on the recorded devel commit. A unique recycling key and zero-length ownership marker isolate the manual test runner. No production config changed. Native TestRunner receipts and the guest scheduler receipt identify the exact SSD worker. One active slot serializes the two fresh fixtures.
method.observer: Trusted QEMU guest agent reads /buildbuddy inside the worker VM. Filesystem totals use df -B1, and outer category totals use one ordered du -sx -B1 invocation with FileCache before remotebuilds so shared inodes count in FileCache. Independent workspace du measures gross blocks.
method.loop_files: File allocation equals Linux st_blocks times stat block unit; filesystem use comes from statfs. The process root is inspected only for the temporary TestRunner ownership marker. tmp workspace backing files are separate from their mounts. Where kubelet bind mounts refer to the same PVC files, the PVC tree is counted once.
method.docker_image_layers: Docker inspect provides DiffIDs. Reconstruct overlay2 ChainIDs and resolve the layerdb cache IDs, then read each layer's diff allocation. These two base image IDs had no shared ChainID; their layer sum is within Docker store allocation.
method.limits: Finite unsynchronized storage reads can miss peaks or observe files changing during scans. Metadata and deleted-but-open files can account for filesystem use outside path sums. The worker PVC figures do not establish physical allocation on the Kubernetes node or backend.

findings.guest_disks: The two 10 GiB KubeVirt workspace files used at most 141 MiB in total. The four guest QCOW2 overlays used less than 1 MiB. Firecracker’s live root copy used 589 MiB. At the busiest observed checkpoint the old RAM snapshot and the new capture together took 3.00 GiB. The live and checkpoint root copies occupied up to 1.72 GiB together.
findings.shared_disk: The unshared BuildBuddy executor and RBE action image layers occupied 1.47 GiB and 1.66 GiB. At the KubeVirt point the worker held 4.21 GiB in the input cache and 9.86 GiB in Docker including the image layers and the runner’s backing file. Docker accounts for the outer backing file once. The inner image stores, PVCs and snapshots occupy blocks within it.
findings.reclaim: Trim Firecracker’s private ext4 after workload cleanup. In one disposable full-suite repeat, trim returned 9.45 GiB of worker allocation in 0.44s (13.65 GiB to 4.20 GiB) with inner free space unchanged. A teardown trim returns space for the next assignment. The trial disposed the runner after trimming. Verify warm reuse after trim and measure runtime peak before changing the disk request.
findings.diagnostic_method: 22 November UTC. Read-only worker samples roughly every nine seconds on one SSD worker. The temporary Docker runner keys forced fresh K3s fixtures while the outer worker could reuse cached data. A TestRunner result confirmed each scenario independently of the outer Bazel result. The first KubeVirt invocation hit a separate Mypy scheduling error. Reported peaks are sampled maxima. QGA reads report guest filesystem allocation. Physical allocation on the storage node is outside this study.

trim_trial.measurement: Across /usr/sbin/fstrim after workload cleanup and before private runner disposal. st_blocks * 512 on the sparse backing determines actual reclaimed allocation; util-linux verbose output measures discard extents submitted.
